question: Is Ascend 910B faster than L40S for this model per card and per quota point, and can its extra 20 GiB of memory be spent on speed?

answer.per_card: 910B is about 11% faster than L40S once its host loader is fed.
answer.per_point: About +5%: 0.35 points/card-hour on 910B against 0.33 on L40S.
answer.extra_memory: No measurable gain. Every configuration that spends the extra memory lands at or below the fully recomputed baseline.
answer.real_bottleneck: The host data pipeline, not the device. Default loader threads left the 910B waiting about 14 s per 28 s step.

method.entry_point: training.train on the published release; no microbenchmark
method.metric: occupied_tokens per second per card = median(occupied_tokens)/cards / seconds
method.statistic: occ/mean is the headline (same statistic as the L40S baseline); occ/median is given because the two disagree inside the noise band
method.per_card_work_held_fixed: global_batch = packs_per_card x cards, one sequence_length window per pack
method.no_silent_fallback: PRETRAIN_REQUIRE_FUSED=1 makes any reference path taken on an NPU tensor raise; summary.json records operator_paths

baseline_l40s.selection: steps 101..824 of the final restart-free segment; the first ~100 steps after a restart are warm-up and were excluded

ascend_910b.node_shape: 16 cards, 180 CPU quota row (192 cores visible)

configurations.name: packs8-wide
configurations.note: best; baseline recompute, 8 packs per card

configurations.name: base-full
configurations.note: same configuration as packs8-wide in a separate job; the pair bounds run-to-run spread at about 0.5%

configurations.name: dit-keep12
configurations.note: spends 19.5 GiB more than baseline and buys 5% off backward, which the slower forward cancels

configurations.name: ditchunk16k
configurations.note: cheapest of the memory-spending knobs and the only one ahead of baseline by median, but inside the noise band

configurations.name: default-loader
configurations.note: the starved measurement this whole investigation started from

conclusions: Feeding the loader is the only change that mattered: data_wait fell from 15.05 s to 0.01 s and the step from 29.98 s to about 21 s at 4 packs per card.

The extra 20 GiB can be spent (dit-keep12 reaches 51.7 GiB) but buys nothing. DiT recompute is only about 5% of backward and about 3% of the step, so trading memory for it is inside the measurement noise.
Partial backbone recompute is actively worse: -6% against baseline.
The memory configurations disagree between mean and median at n=10, which is itself the evidence that their differences are not resolvable. Only the n=38 and n=724 runs support a claim.
keep_attention_activations has no headroom: its ceiling is layers // full_attention_interval = 24/4 = 6, which production already uses.
--micro-batch is not an axis for real data; training/configure.py rejects any value but 1.
untested: The Wan DiT pointwise chain (modulated_norm, gated_add) still runs its reference expression on both backends. The Ascend fusion is TorchAIR, which cannot be enabled on this stack: Dynamo's device check reads a None compute capability from torch_npu and raises TypeError on 'None >= 7'.
Multi-node 910B scaling. Every number here is one 16-card node, against 32 L40S cards on four nodes, so L40S carries inter-node allreduce cost that Ascend does not.
